strings.name: Kara Walker
strings.role: Artist · Silhouettes, installations and public sculpture
strings.summary: Walker moved from black silhouettes to film, monumental sculpture and mechanical installations, examining slavery, race, sexuality and violence through alluring yet disturbing images. She places historical narratives alongside viewers' desires; her use of stereotypes has also provoked debate. Recent colored collages and automatons continue her investigation of historical memory.
strings.coverageNote: Selected verifiable milestones through 16 November 2026; not a live news archive.
strings.influence.rationale: Uses silhouettes, installations and public sculpture to examine slavery, race and gender, sustaining contemporary art's scrutiny of historical violence.
strings.facts.f1.label: Birthplace
strings.facts.f1.value: Stockton, California; raised in Atlanta from age thirteen.
strings.facts.f2.label: Education
strings.facts.f2.value: BFA from Atlanta College of Art in 1991; MFA from RISD in 1994.
strings.highlights.h1.title: Historical conflict in silhouette
strings.highlights.h1.text: Arranges racialized images, sexuality and power into unsettling historical scenes using cut paper.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Remaking public monuments
strings.highlights.h2.text: From a sugar sphinx to automatons, uses scale, materials and theater to reconsider trauma.
strings.timeline.t1.title: New collage exhibition in Berlin
strings.timeline.t1.text: Dispatches from A— reworked American historical imagery through colored cutouts, watercolor and ink.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Presented the Fortuna installation
strings.timeline.t2.text: SFMOMA commissioned automatons in an obsidian setting to consider trauma, technology and transformation.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Fons Americanus in London
strings.timeline.t3.text: The monumental fountain in Tate's Turbine Hall reimagined imperial monuments and Atlantic history.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Public project in a sugar refinery
strings.timeline.t4.text: A Subtlety used a giant sugar-covered sculpture in Brooklyn's former refinery to address sugar and exploitation.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Career survey began touring
strings.timeline.t5.text: Walker Art Center organized a major show that later traveled to the Whitney and other institutions.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Received a MacArthur fellowship
strings.timeline.t6.text: Her early silhouette practice gained interdisciplinary support and wider debate.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Breakthrough exhibition
strings.timeline.t7.text: After her RISD MFA, showed the large silhouette work Gone… at New York's Drawing Center.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Completed her BFA
strings.timeline.t8.text: Trained in Atlanta before continuing graduate study at RISD.
